exposure: HOIP gene mutations (c.1654 C > T, p.Gln552Ter; c.3038 A > C, p.His1013Pro)
outcome: Reduced central memory (CD8 CM) T cells
Reduced effector memory (CD8 EM) T cells
Higher percentage of naive B cells
Lower percentage of memory B cells
Impaired NF-kB phosphorylation in T and B cells
cohort: A 1-year-6-month-old Chinese boy with early-onset autoinflammation and immunodeficiency was studied.
finding: Novel compound heterozygous HOIP mutations lead to multiple immune abnormalities, impaired NF-kB activation, and activation of the type I interferon pathway.
